text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A bill mandating eight years of uninterrupted secularist education bill is working its way slowly through a parliamentary commission.
- Former general who lead the 1980 miliatry coup says he would appear in an advertisement for a clothing company if the firm doantes $4,000 to a new foundation he is creating.
- Power deliveries to residential areas will be cut at night.
- Police officials say 2,161 people died in traffic accidents in the first half of 1997.
- President Suleyman Demirel ratifies a law to close down casinos, widely blamed in media reports for laundering mafia money.
- The corpses of two dead Kurdistan Workers Party militants were displayed in the streets of southeastern province of Hakkari after a recent clash.
- The Islam-based Welfare Party, facing possible closure by the courts, has begun secret preparations to create a successor party.
- Twenty Islamists in the western city of Izmit were arrested for holding an illegal demostration and for insulting the secularist founder of Turkey, Kemal Ataturk.
